extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and practitioners in NLP/ML for regulatory compliance, architects, compliance engineers, and built-environment AI researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate and deploy GPT-4.0 (and LLMs) to detect ambiguities, contradictions, and conflicting requirements in regulatory document corpora (particularly building regulations), using curated datasets, human-expert ground truth, and standard IR/NLP evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in detecting inconsistencies (precision/recall/F1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use metrics such as precision, recall, and F1 score to measure the model's accuracy in detecting conflicts and inconsistencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The experiment demonstrates GPT-4.0’s effectiveness using precision, recall, and F1 score; flagged inconsistencies are compared against a ground truth established by experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground-truth creation via curated corpus with injected inconsistencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Design experiments using a curated corpus where deliberate ambiguities, contradictions, and conflicting requirements are artificially injected to create a known ground truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Injected inconsistencies were designed in collaboration with architects and compliance engineers to reflect common issues found in regulatory texts; the model's outputs are measured against this ground truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human expert validation of model findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Flagged inconsistencies must be reviewed and validated by human experts to assess correctness and practical relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The flagged inconsistencies have been reviewed by human experts to validate the model's findings and assess practicality for real-world tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure input fits model context/window constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprocess documents so that the text input fits within the LLM's maximum context size (e.g., GPT-4.0's 128k-token window).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected text was converted from PDF to text and chosen to fit within GPT-4.0's maximum context size (128 thousand tokens) so the model can process the entire document in one pass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document preprocessing (PDF→text and corpus search/extraction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert PDFs to text and use semantic/document search to extract relevant regulations and guidance from the corpus before LLM processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: i-ReC supports corpus search and extraction of relevant regulations (building regs, legislation, Approved Documents); documents were converted from PDF to text for input to GPT-4.0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison to baseline systems / search engines
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate LLM/system performance against existing baselines (e.g., BSOL) and prior systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: i-ReC's semantic search engine was validated against existing search engines like BSI’s BSOL and found far superior in representative scenarios; similar baseline comparisons should be used when assessing LLM approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation with knowledge graphs for symbolic reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Use knowledge graphs (KGs) to formally capture regulatory knowledge to enable symbolic reasoning and support downstream processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KGs have been used to capture regulatory knowledge to enable symbolic reasoning; the research integrates NLP with Semantic Web approaches (i-ReC platform).

rubrics_metrics.name: Address common corpus challenges (ambiguity, inconsistent terms, synonyms, contradictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems should handle inconsistent use of terms, ambiguities, synonyms, conflicting requirements, and lack of clarity intrinsic to regulatory corpora.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corpus suffers from inconsistent use of terms, ambiguities, contradictions and lack of clarity necessitating interpretations of requirements; experiments inject and test for these phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompting and in-context learning strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and apply prompting techniques and in-context/few-shot learning strategies (e.g., chain-of-thought, self-consistency, self-reflection) to improve LLM performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior work explored ICL/few-shot learning and prompting strategies including CoT prompting, self-consistency, and self-reflection; these strategies can be used to improve translations/detections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of API-driven experimental workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Interface the LLM via its API for automated, repeatable experiments (feeding modified regulatory text and collecting responses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The experiment involves feeding modified regulatory text into GPT-4.0 through its API and tasking the model with identifying planted inconsistencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain-specific fine-tuning or specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine-tune models for particular regulatory domains (e.g., fire safety, structural integrity, environmental regulations) to increase accuracy and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Future work will prioritize fine-tuning the model for specific regulatory domains to enhance accuracy and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and dataset diversity for robust evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale experiments to include larger and more diverse regulatory document sets to better assess generality and limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Future work will focus on scaling up experiments to include larger and more diverse sets of regulatory documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated conflict resolution (suggesting solutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond detection, systems should aim to suggest resolutions or reconciliations for identified inconsistencies using generative capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A key area of development is automated conflict resolution, leveraging GPT-4.0's generative capabilities to not only detect but also suggest solutions for identified inconsistencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-world applicability assessment via pilot projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the tool's practical utility and impact in operational compliance scenarios through pilot projects with industry partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The impact of the tool in real-world compliance scenarios will be assessed through pilot projects with industry partners, gathering empirical data to evaluate effectiveness and utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use expert-informed injection to reflect realistic ambiguity patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating test cases, replicate common real-world ambiguity/contradiction patterns as identified by domain experts to ensure ecological validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate ambiguities and contradictions were injected reflecting some of the common issues found in regulatory texts; these were designed with architects and compliance engineers.
